raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With HiCache `write_back`, a device eviction has to wait for the forward that is running on the device (the write fence) before it can copy its victims to the host pool. `evict_for_alloc` frees only what the allocation is short of, so a busy prefill server evicts many small batches and pays that wait each time. In a PP4 prefill (GLM-5.2, 8K-token chunks, host pool 250 GB per rank), one scheduler spent about 35% of its time in `writing_check`, 79% of it waiting for the forward to end, and the GPU idled about 46% between steps.

## Modifications

- `environ.py`: new `SGLANG_HICACHE_EVICT_HEADROOM_TOKENS` (`EnvInt`, default 0 = off).
- `unified_radix_cache.py` `evict_for_alloc`: when the policy is `write_back` and the request asks for fewer full-KV tokens than the value (and more than 0), the request is raised to the value, so one call frees a larger batch. The extra victims are demoted to the host pool and stay available as prefix cache. SWA / Mamba requests, `allocation_reclaim_satisfied` calls and non-`write_back` policies are untouched.
- Unit test: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_evict_headroom.py` (off by default; small request raised; large request, zero full-KV request and non-`write_back` unchanged).

## Accuracy Tests

The victims are chosen by the existing walk and written back by the existing path; only the target size changes. Checked on a v0.5.22-based build (MI355X, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, 1 prefill TP1 x PP4 + 1 decode TP4/DP4, value 524288) with a capped-pool gate: device pool limited to 300K tokens per rank so evictions are continuous and a second 16k x 128 pass loads the host copies back.

| | knob off (control) | knob 524288 |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 200-prompt probe | 0.965 | 0.975 |
| garbled outputs | 4 | 4 |
| long-context needle, 16k x 128 | clean | clean |

The default-size pool never evicts in the normal correctness suites, so only this capped-pool run exercises the path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same build, AgentX trace replay at concurrency 104, 1 hour:

| | knob off | knob 524288 |
|---|---|---|
| tok/s/GPU | 48,360 | 49,807 and 49,631 (+2.8% mean) |
| evictions per prefill step | 1.16 | 0.11 |
| PP0 time spent in eviction (1 h) | 1,686 s | 525 s |
| median full-chunk step | 380 ms | 328 ms |
| prefix-cache hit | same | same |

Limits and caveats:
- The extra victims are kept only if the host pool has room; when it is full, `write_back` drops them (the existing "dropped without backup" path). The dropped counter stayed 0 in these runs.
- One model, one topology (PP prefill), one GPU type. The gain depends on how often evictions happen and how long the write fence waits.
- The runs above used the same logic as an environment variable on the v0.5.22-based build, without the `is_write_back` condition added here (write_back was always on there, so the condition does not change those runs). On current `main` I could run the new unit test but not the end-to-end benchmark.
- A deeper fix would remove the fence wait itself. I tried a background pre-write-back of the oldest victims: evictions became nearly free, but end-to-end throughput did not improve in this setup, so it is not proposed here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code (`ruff format`, `ruff check` pass on the changed files).
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (these `SGLANG_HICACHE_*` variables are not documented elsewhere).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

@@ -877,6 +877,10 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_HICACHE_HF3FS_CONFIG_PATH = EnvStr(None)
     SGLANG_HICACHE_DECODE_OFFLOAD_STRIDE = EnvInt(None)
     SGLANG_HICACHE_SKIP_HOST_DUPLICATE_RECLAIM = EnvBool(False)
+    # Minimum tokens one write_back eviction call frees (0 = off). A write_back eviction waits
+    # for the running forward to finish before copying its victims to host, so one larger
+    # batch is cheaper than many small ones; the extra victims stay in the host pool.
+    SGLANG_HICACHE_EVICT_HEADROOM_TOKENS = EnvInt(0)
     SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR = EnvStr(None)
     # File-backend LRU eviction (opt-in; sizes accept SI/IEC suffixes, "0" disables).
     SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_MAX_SIZE = EnvStr(None)

@@ -776,6 +776,12 @@ def evict_for_alloc(
                 params, allocation_reclaim_satisfied=allocation_reclaim_satisfied
             )
 
+        headroom = envs.SGLANG_HICACHE_EVICT_HEADROOM_TOKENS.get()
+        if self.is_write_back and 0 < params.num_tokens < headroom:
+            # A write_back eviction waits for the running forward (write fence) before it
+            # can copy victims to host, so free one larger batch per call instead of many
+            # small ones. The extra victims are demoted to the host pool.
+            params = replace(params, num_tokens=headroom)
         request_by_type = self._evict_request_by_type(params)
         available_size_targets = {
             ct: (ct, self._component_available_size(ct) + request_cnt)

@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+"""SGLANG_HICACHE_EVICT_HEADROOM_TOKENS raises small write_back eviction requests."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import EvictParams
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedRadixCache
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _Captured(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, params):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.params = params
+
+
+class TestHiCacheEvictHeadroom(CustomTestCase):
+    def _evict_params_seen(self, *, headroom, is_write_back=True, **params):
+        cache = SimpleNamespace(disable=False, is_write_back=is_write_back)
+
+        def capture(evict_params):
+            raise _Captured(evict_params)
+
+        # Stop right after the headroom decision, before any allocator access.
+        cache._evict_request_by_type = capture
+        with envs.SGLANG_HICACHE_EVICT_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(headroom):
+            with self.assertRaises(_Captured) as ctx:
+                UnifiedRadixCache.evict_for_alloc(cache, EvictParams(**params))
+        return ctx.exception.params
+
+    def test_off_by_default(self):
+        seen = self._evict_params_seen(headroom=0, num_tokens=100)
+        self.assertEqual(seen.num_tokens, 100)
+
+    def test_small_request_is_raised(self):
+        seen = self._evict_params_seen(headroom=4096, num_tokens=100, swa_num_tokens=7)
+        self.assertEqual(seen.num_tokens, 4096)
+        self.assertEqual(seen.swa_num_tokens, 7)
+
+    def test_large_request_is_kept(self):
+        seen = self._evict_params_seen(headroom=4096, num_tokens=10000)
+        self.assertEqual(seen.num_tokens, 10000)
+
+    def test_no_full_token_request_is_kept(self):
+        seen = self._evict_params_seen(headroom=4096, num_tokens=0, mamba_num=3)
+        self.assertEqual(seen.num_tokens, 0)
+
+    def test_only_with_write_back(self):
+        seen = self._evict_params_seen(
+            headroom=4096, is_write_back=False, num_tokens=100
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(seen.num_tokens, 100)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
